Theme

Latin word

excitō

excitō, excitāre, excitāvī, excitātum

verb, first conjugation, transitive

rouse, stir up, call forth (a feeling, laughter, interest); wake up: switch on (a phone, a computer); wake, rouse (from sleep)

In this lexicon

  • excite

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fam. 3.11.3: quōs ego rīsūs excitāssem!; Traupman 152, 150; Traupman 288; Traupman 311

  • switch on

    the recommended word · modern · Traupman 262, s.v. turn on; Andresian pp. 14–15; Traupman 262, 399

  • wake someone up

    also used · classical · Liv. 5.47.3: nē canēs quidem … excitārent; Cic. Rep. 6.12: nē mē ē somnō excitētis (Lewis & Short); Traupman 39, 403: wake up, tr., (ē somnō) excitāre

Examples

  • mihi ille dētur puer, quem laus excitet, quem glōria juvet, quī victus fleat

    give me the boy whom praise fires up, who loves glory, who cries when he losesQuīnt. 1.3.7

    In the entry for excite

  • honōs alit artēs, omnēsque incenduntur ad studia glōriā

    honour feeds the arts, and everyone is fired to effort by gloryCic. Tusc. 1.4

    In the entry for excite

  • mē miserum, quī nōn adfuerim! quōs ego rīsūs excitāssem!

    too bad I wasn’t there! what laughs I’d have raised!Cic. Fam. 3.11.3
